move: footage posterised to editorial palettes, hard cuts with grain surges
how: A 640x360 canvas paints procedural footage (sunset sky, sun, three parallax ridges, shimmering sea, a walking figure) with a slow pan on a sine over D. Each frame the pixels are mapped by luminance plus seeded grain to one of three five-colour palettes (rust, blue, violet); the loop is cut into thirds, and at each cut the palette hard-switches, grain surges (exponential spikes either side of the cut) and the level count re-opens from 2 to 5 colours over the first 70% of the segment. Five swatches at bottom right show the active palette and which levels are open; a serif caption reads as a magazine issue.
adapt: Feed the product footage into the source canvas (same-origin), replace the three palettes with brand colour sets, the caption text and swatch styling. Keep the grain surge on each cut and the 2 to 5 level opening, which is the editorial rhythm.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the low-res canvas and swatches; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate paints the footage, clamps it and updates the swatches, replacing fx.register. The seeded per-frame rng must use frame index, not Math.random.
caveats: sea shimmer and figure legs use raw t so they are not periodic, but the loop boundary is one of the hard palette cuts so the mismatch is hidden
